audit.why: 55.95% over 2438 games is Annie-favoured, yet difficulty is rated 7/10. That is defensible rather than contradictory: the lane is winnable but punishing, since a single mistimed step into Sweeping Blade range with no stack ends it.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[].side read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yasuo while win[] read Skill/Skill/Skill/Annie/Annie/Yasuo/Annie.
audit.why: Four rows disagreed. win[] matches packet.levelChart exactly and matches the phase whys — phases[6].why literally describes Annie flipping late fights while its side said Yasuo.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly claims Wind Wall blocks Annie's Q and her stun cast ('Windwall can block a single stun-charging auto or Q', 'Avoid casting your stun through his wall'). The full layer's tldr says the opposite.
audit.why: Riot's text for Disintegrate is 'Annie hurls a Mana infused fireball' at a target — it is a targeted spell, not a skillshot, and Wind Wall blocks projectiles. The kit file's 'projectile' derived flag on Annie's Q is a tooltip-parsing misfire; the brief instructs trusting the description over the flag. Wind Wall does stop her basic attacks, which is what actually costs her a Pyromania stack. The two layers currently give a paying user opposite instructions.
audit.corrected: Content layer corrected to match the true interaction: the wall eats autos, not the targeted Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall was called 'matchup-defining' with no cooldown, and Sweeping Blade's re-cast restriction was never mentioned.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s for a 4-second wall — a 21-second window every cycle. Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for several seconds, so a Yasuo who dashes onto Annie cannot immediately dash back off her.
audit.corrected: Both written into breakdown.cooldowns and the trade advice.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0].d gave a generic reason for avoiding extended trades.
audit.why: The real reason is Way of the Wanderer: his shield builds whenever he is moving, so a long trade keeps refilling the thing you are trying to break through.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave used the generic 'every assassin timer in the game' template.
audit.why: Yasuo's specific punish on a shoved wave is Steel Tempest clearing it and Sweeping Blade using the minions as dash targets to reach her.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Molten Shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Yasuo Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 4 seconds long — it eats your autos, never your targeted Q, so keep stunning through it. - Sweeping Blade cannot re-cast onto the same target, so once he dashes to you he is stuck in your radius.

edits.before: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: It eats autos for four seconds but never your targeted Q — stun through the wall and save the autos for after it expires.

edits.before: Yasuo whiffs Wind Wall and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Yasuo whiffs Wind Wall — 25 seconds of lane belongs to you.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: His passive shield rebuilds whenever he moves — long trades only refill it.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry off his commitment — a Yasuo who dashed in cannot Sweeping Blade back onto you, so that is your radius.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-refund farmed wave you never push past river — your kill threat is Flash radius, not wave state. Worst wave: a shoved wave with zero stacks and Tibbers down — every assassin timer in the game points at that picture. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. edits.after: Best wave: a Q-refund farmed wave you never push past river — your kill threat is Flash radius, not wave state. Worst wave: a shoved wave with zero stacks and Tibbers down — Yasuo clears it with Steel Tempest and dashes off those minions straight onto you. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.

edits.before: Yasuo's Windwall can block a single stun-charging auto or Q if timed right, but he has no reliable way to punish you at range before that, so early trades favor whoever plays the poke-and-wall guessing game better.
edits.after: Wind Wall stops your autos but never your targeted Q, so the stun still lands through it, and he has no ranged punish either — early trades come down to who respects the 25-second wall cooldown less.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are an even skill matchup — Yasuo's Windwall counters a single stun but he can't punish Annie from range otherwise
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are an even skill matchup — Wind Wall eats her autos but not her targeted Q, and he cannot punish from range

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are an even matchup — Yasuo's Windwall can shut down a single stun cast, but he has no way to punish you from range beforehand, so trades depend on timing and positioning rather than one side having a clear kit advantage.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even — Wind Wall blocks your autos but not your targeted Q, so the stun still lands, and he has no ranged punish beforehand; trades depend on timing and positioning rather than either kit holding a clear advantage.

edits.before: Farm safely and use Windwall reactively to block incoming stuns/poke
edits.after: Farm safely and use Wind Wall reactively to block her autos and Tibbers

notes: The two layers actively contradicted each other on the central interaction: full.tldr correctly said Wind Wall cannot block point-and-click, while four content strings told the reader the wall blocks her Q and stun. Corrected the content side. Note that Annie's Q carries a 'projectile' derived flag in the kit file that contradicts Riot's own targeted-cast description — flagged here because that same misfire will affect every Annie matchup against a projectile-blocker. Four level-chart rows disagreed and were realigned to the packet chart as one group.
